A WebVisu screen keeps its hiding and its alarm colors when it comes over, and any symbol on any screen can now be shown and painted by a rule on a tag. A small fix to the backup list rides along. Built for amd64 only; the multi-arch build follows as the next version.

## What changed

- **A symbol can be shown and painted by rules.** `show` draws a symbol only while a rule on a tag holds, so a door, a guard or a pump drawn for one state is there only in that state. `colors` is up to four rules, each with a tone (`ok`, `warn`, `bad` or `info`): the first one that holds paints the symbol in that tone, and when none holds it is drawn as it was. A rule is a tag and a comparison (`on`, `off`, `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `ge`, `lt`, `le`). A rule whose tag has no good reading holds nothing and hides nothing, so a lost connection never makes a symbol vanish. The symbols form in the builder has both, and a screen file lists and moves the rules' tags with the rest. See [Dashboards](/iot/dashboards/).
- **The CODESYS screen import carries Invisible and Toggle color.** An element's Invisible variable (its group's too) becomes a `show` rule, with `NOT x` turning it over, and its Toggle color variable becomes a `colors` rule in the tone nearest the element's own alarm color. They are found at the ids the CODESYS IDE's own element trees give them. What it cannot carry is said in the import, with the variable: these two on a shape drawn into the background picture (a pipe, a vessel, a frame), because the picture is one image, and every other variable-driven setting (a fill, frame or text color, a movement, a blink, a text list). See [Import a CODESYS screen](/iot/codesys-screen-import/).
- **The backup list does not fail while a backup is pruned.** The scheduled backup prunes old backups on its own goroutine, and a list that landed in the middle failed on the missing file, which the API answered as a server error. A backup that went is now left out of the list.

## Migrations

None.

## API changes

A symbol's configuration takes `show` and `colors`. No route changed. See [the HTTP API](/iot/api/).

## Upgrading from 4.23.2

A plain `helm upgrade`. No migration and no new secret. A symbol with neither rule is drawn as before.

## What is not proven

- The CODESYS import was proven against the IDE's own export of one visualization and the CODESYS Refrigerator example's group variable. A screen from another project may list more it could not place.
- The new symbol rules were proven by the suite's tests, not on a plant's screen.
